title: ERS-EO NEW PRODUCT DEVELOPMENTS: AGENTIC AI FOR EO IN PPDR - EXPRO+
description: As part of the European Resilience from Space - Earth Observation (ERS-EO) Programme Element 2, this tender covers the development and demonstration of new Earth Observation (EO)-based products supported by agentic artificial intelligence for Public Protection and Disaster Relief (PPDR). Each contract will have a maximum value of 2 million and an expected duration of 24 months.The activities will develop suites of new EO-based products adapted to the needs of PPDR users. The products will use satellite imagery as a primary input and combine it with complementary data sources. They will be benchmarked against existing solutions to demonstrate improvements in areas such as accuracy, timeliness, coverage and ease of use.Each activity will also develop an agentic AI engine supporting the discovery, integration, benchmarking and recommendation of EO products and data. The developed capabilities will include reusable interfaces and a user workspace with an AI copilot and will be demonstrated with representative PPDR users. Product operationalisation is outside the scope of the activities.The Agency intends to select up to four (4) proposals, to be implemented through separate contracts. Each proposal shall address at least one of the following PPDR user groups and may address more than one:(1) Civil protection and emergency management;(2) Law enforcement;(3) Fire and rescue; and(4) Border and coast guard.In selecting the overall portfolio, the Agency will seek broad and complementary coverage of these PPDR user groups. The complementarity of proposals and the avoidance of unnecessary duplication between the user communities addressed may therefore be taken into account in the selection.This tender is addressed to economic operators from countries participating in ERS-EO Programme Element 2. The placement and distribution of contracts will be subject to the availability of funding under the applicable national programme subscriptions.The key tasks and outputs are expected to include:(1) Definition of PPDR use cases, requirements and fitness-for-use criteria;(2) Development and benchmarking of new EO-based products combining satellite imagery with complementary data;(3) Development of an agentic AI engine, reusable interfaces and a user workspace;(4) Verification, validation, security and assurance activities;(5) Demonstration and evaluation with representative PPDR users; and(6) Preparation of a roadmap for possible future integration into Space Resilience Node environments.

title: LARGE ANGLE FLEXURE PIVOT WITH INTEGRATED CONSTANT TORQUE MECHANISM -EXPRO+
description: Objective: To incorporate Constant Torque Mechanisms into Large Angle Flexure Pivot mechanisms in order to reduce driving torque requirements and power needed to operate the mechanism and maximise angular motion range of flexible pivot with Constant Torque Mechanism.Description: This activity aims to integrate Large Angle Flexure Pivot (LAFP) mechanisms with innovative Constant Torque Mechanisms (CTMs) to reduce the torque/force required for actuation. Previous developments on flexural pivots have demonstrated their suitability for high-precision and lubrication-free applications; however, actuation remains a limiting factor for large-angle movements. This activity focuses on addressing this limitation through the use of CTMs. The development of a dedicated actuator is explicitly excluded from the scope. The combination of CTMs with LAFPs provides a promising alternative to traditional rigid-body hinges and standalone compliant pivots. This hybrid approach aims to maintain the benefits of compliant mechanismssuch as zero backlash and inter-element gaps, high precision, absence of lubrication, and reduced wear debris due to elastic deformationwhile reducing actuation effort. These properties are particularly relevant for long-duration space missions and fine-pointing applications, where high-precision and reliability are critical. The integration of CTMs is expected to improve the stability of the flexures while reducing actuation force (and power needed to operate them), making them more competitive and suitable for long-term space missions. Additionally, a key innovation under consideration is a dual-mode functionality, enabling the mechanism to switch between a compliant mode and a stiff configuration. This feature would allow the mechanism to remain locked during launch and operate flexibly in orbit. The flexible pivot with an integrated Constant Torque Mechanism would find application in high-stability pointing mechanisms for optical payloads and pointing mechanisms. The key benefits include reduced actuation torque (and power requirements) and the potential implementation of bi-stable stiffness, which could be adjusted to secure compliant components during launch. This would be added value on top of other benefits of using compliant mechanisms for pointing applications such as lack of lubrication, reduced contamination and precise motion etc. The tasks foreseen in this activity include: - Concept definition and literature review. Assess existing CTM designs and develop initial concepts for large angle flex pivot with integrated CTM. - Breadboard design of the integrated CTM-Flexure mechanism. - Breadboard manufacturing of Large Angle Flexure Pivot with Integrated Constant Torque Mechanism - Characterisation and functional testing to validate torque reduction and stiffness adjustment capabilities. And verify that the expected motion range can be safely achieved. - Roadmap for TRL advancementDeliverables: Breadboard, ReportProcurement Policy: C(1) = Activities in open competition limited to the-non-Large-System Integrators. title: REACTION CONTROL SYSTEM THRUSTER FED WITH GASES FROM CRYOGENIC PROPELLANTS - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a breadboard of a reaction control system thruster, fed with gaseous methane or hydrogen and gaseous oxygen, as part of a unified propulsion system with a main engine fed by LOX/LH2/LCH4.Description: In the last decade, alternative propellants for space exploration have become a tangible reality, with more and more companies investing in new propellant combinations. Currently, some of the most promising propellant combinations include Oxygen, Hydrogen and Methane. These propellants show potential to be used for gaseous fed reaction control system (RCS) thrusters. RCS thrusters enable attitude control or main thrust capability for small spacecrafts, without the use of a separate propulsion system. This activity tests the new propellant combinations in RCS thrusters. Such thruster could enable higher performance than storable propellants. As well, Oxygen, Methane and Hydrogen can be sourced or produced on other planets (ISRU, e.g. Mars, Moon) which could enable new exploration mission scenarios. This development designs and preliminary tests an RCS thruster that is fed by gaseous oxygen as oxydiser and either gaseous methane or gaseous hydrogen asfuel. The thrusters requirements shall be in line with selected use cases of exploration missions (e.g. lunar lander or interplanetary vehicle). This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Perform a trade-off on propellant selection (considering i.e. GOX/GH2or GOX/GCH4), thrust of the main thruster, and scaled up and down version for preliminary study (i.e. 100N - 500N). - Perform preliminary design, investigating pulsed operation (and necessary ignition technology) - Design, manufacture and test a breadboard model of an RCS thruster, including functional tests - Perform a preliminary study on thrust scalability

title: SELF-DEFENDED, AUTONOMOUSLY SECURE SPACECRAFTS - EXPRO PLUS
description: Objective: To develop and implement a proof of concept of a self-defended, autonomously secure spacecraft.Description: ESA Vision is to move towards highly autonomous systems in order to revolutionize space missions. To achieve this, there is a need to automate also the security functions and self-defense of the spacecraft itself. In addition to an activity on Intelligent Space Systems, thisactivity is complementary by filling the gap on security aspects. The very large number of satellites, the dense and complicated geopolitical environment, as well as the concept of highly autonomous systems themselves make it necessary to also invest on the self-defense of the satellites themselves. To implement autonomous space missions, spacecrafts must automate all the security functions, e.g. key management, that allows them to operate securely without intervention from ground segment operators. In addition, spacecrafts need to maintain a Space Situational Awareness (SSA), which involves the comprehensive monitoring, tracking, and analysis of objects and activities in space, including potential malicious ones. The information collected through on-board sensors must me automatically tracked, analysed, identified, correlated and categorised on board, enabling detection, prediction, warning and triggering of automated reaction for mitigation or secure spacecraft restoration when needed. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Perform a state-off-the-art on space intelligent platforms and on spacecraft autonomous systems - Based on space security reference architecture, and threat analysis, identify security services to be automated and technologies that need to be developed to implement aself-defense spacecraft - Design an architecture for autonomously secure, self defense spacecrafts - Develop a proof-of-concept in a simulated environment, where basic spacecraft security functions are automated, information from (simulated or emulated) sensors is collected, analysed, correlated, and categorised, while security measures implemented on board are triggered, incl. automatically reconfiguration to restore secure operations. - Test the proof-of-concept based on pre-defined scenarios - Identify gaps and proposeroadmap for further evolution Software shall be delivered under an ESA Software Community License, so that any individuals or entities within ESA Member States can access to it and can provide update to the community of users.
